AfterShuffle.issue: Rollup of guard N4 per binding rule 4. The effect, the owner guard and the constant all match and the trigger set is executed-confirmed identical (N3); the one divergence is that C# refuses to dispatch AfterShuffle once the combat is over or ending (CardPileCmd.cs:866-869, :897-900, :915-918 -- three separate guards) and the sim's on_shuffle has no such gate.

guards.rationale: Multiplayer-only owner disambiguation. The shared contract lists multiplayer-only params as out of scope; the sim's single Player makes the check structurally true. Hook.AfterShuffle passes the shuffling Player (Hook.cs:1130-1135), so in single-player the check can only ever be true; the sim keeps it anyway, which is the right shape for when it matters. Recorded rather than skipped because the sibling AfterShuffle implementer BiiigHug.cs:30 carries the identical guard and the sim's relics/biiig_hug.py should read the same way.

guards.what: N2: BlockVar(6m, ValueProp.Unpowered) (TheAbacus.cs:17) vs BLOCK = 6 with props=ValueProp.UNPOWERED (the_abacus.py:20, 25)
guards.rationale: No AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension in the file, so 6 is the pinned non-ascension value, and the Unpowered typing is carried into BlockCmd.apply -- which matters because is_powered_attack(props) is what gates the sim's block modifiers (valueprops.py:47-49). `CreatureCmd.GainBlock(base.Owner.Creature, base.DynamicVars.Block, null)` (TheAbacus.cs:26) passes cardSource = null and the sim's call passes no card either, so no card-sourced block modifier can attach to it on either side.

guards.what: N3 (EXECUTED -- settles the trigger set, which is the only interesting question this relic has): which shuffles fire AfterShuffle
guards.rationale: Hook.AfterShuffle has exactly ONE dispatch site in the whole game -- CardPileCmd.cs:917, at the bottom of CardPileCmd.Shuffle -- so it fires from the explicit Shuffle command and from ShuffleIfNecessary (CardPileCmd.cs:972-981, which calls Shuffle only when the draw pile is empty and the discard pile is not), and NOT from the combat-start randomise, which is a different call path (CardPile.RandomizeOrderInternal). The sim's on_shuffle has exactly three call sites: player.py:218 (reshuffle_discard_into_draw = the ShuffleIfNecessary path), player.py:239 (shuffle_draw_and_discard = the explicit Shuffle) and cards/havoc.py:42 (Havoc's inline ShuffleIfNecessary, whose C# counterpart also routes through Shuffle). The sets match. EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b16.py abacus-shuffle`): 0 block at combat start with the relic attached, 6 block after a ShuffleIfNecessary reshuffle -- exactly the C# numbers. Rule 7: player.py, cards/havoc.py and CardPileCmd.cs are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N4: C# skips the AfterShuffle dispatch entirely when the combat is over or ending; the sim's on_shuffle has no is_over gate
guards.issue: MECHANISM: CardPileCmd.Shuffle returns immediately on `CombatManager.Instance.IsOverOrEnding` (CardPileCmd.cs:866-869), bails out mid-way through its card-add loop on the same condition (:897-900), and wraps the hook itself in `if (!CombatManager.Instance.IsOverOrEnding)` (:915-918), so a shuffle triggered by a dying effect grants no Abacus block. PlayerCombatState.reshuffle_discard_into_draw fires hooks.on_shuffle(self) unconditionally (player.py:218) and the_abacus.py:22-25 adds no gate of its own -- contrast relics/unceasing_top.py:23, which does check `not self.combat.is_over`, so the sim has the idiom. REACHABILITY (DORMANT): reaching it needs a reshuffle after the combat is decided. The sim reshuffles only from PlayerCombatState._draw (player.py:285) and combat.py:493-494 breaks the play loop once the combat is decided, so no ported effect draws after the last enemy dies. Porting any on-death or combat-end effect that draws (or an explicit Shuffle at combat end) makes it live; the observable is block on a player who has already won, which matters for the conformance runner's player-state assertions rather than for combat outcomes. Filed as a gap rather than a waiver because 'no ported effect reaches it' is today's content, not the divergence's shape (binding rule 1). Rule 7: player.py, combat.py, relics/unceasing_top.py and CardPileCmd.cs are not hashed here.
